subUnits.title: 2.1 Description Physique et Personnelle (Complete Self-Description)
notes: Description Physique et Personnelle
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: combine physical and personal description into a complete, fluent self-description.
Key Concepts:
1. A Complete Self-Description Combines:
- Physical build (ÊTRE): je suis grand(e) / petit(e) / mince
- Hair (AVOIR): j'ai les cheveux [colour/texture]
- Character (ÊTRE): je suis honnête / timide / courageux(se), etc.
2. Fluency — Switching Between Être and Avoir:
- ÊTRE is used for core identity/traits described directly.
- AVOIR is used for POSSESSED features described with a noun (like hair).
- A fluent speaker moves between these AUTOMATICALLY, without hesitation.
- COMMON ERROR: 'je suis les cheveux longs' — this uses être where avoir is needed.
Formula Box:
je suis grand(e) — ÊTRE for build/character
j'ai les cheveux courts et noirs — AVOIR for possessed features
je suis honnête et un peu timide — ÊTRE for character
Analogy:

Moving fluently between être and avoir within one description is like a skilled driver smoothly changing gears while driving, without needing to stop and think about each gear change consciously — exactly the fluency we are building this week.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Using ONLY être throughout a description, incorrectly applying it to hair ('je suis les cheveux longs' instead of 'j'ai les cheveux longs').
- Losing agreement consistency when switching between different sentence types.

quiz.q: A complete self-description typically includes ___.
opts: no particular content; anything at all works equally
quiz.explanation: A well-rounded self-description includes physical build, hair, and character — using both être and avoir.

quiz.q: Which verb is used for physical build, like 'I am tall'?
quiz.explanation: 'Être' is used for physical build: je suis grand(e).

quiz.q: Which verb is used for hair, like 'I have black hair'?
quiz.explanation: 'Avoir' is used for possessed features like hair: j'ai les cheveux noirs.

quiz.q: Which verb is used for character, like 'I am honest'?
quiz.explanation: 'Être' is used for character traits: je suis honnête.

quiz.q: This week's focus is on developing ___.
opts: fluency, moving smoothly between être and avoir sentences
a single, isolated new grammar rule
quiz.explanation: The key skill is fluency — switching automatically between être (build/character) and avoir (hair) within the same description.

quiz.q: A fluent speaker selects the correct verb and agreement ___.
opts: never; fluency has no connection to grammar
only after extensive, slow, conscious translation each time
almost automatically, through familiarity from practice
quiz.explanation: Fluency is built through repeated practice until verb selection and agreement become nearly automatic.

quiz.q: This week's analogy compares fluent verb-switching to ___.
opts: a beginner driver who never changes gears
a skilled driver smoothly changing gears
driving with no connection to skill level
quiz.explanation: A skilled driver changes gears automatically — just as a fluent French speaker switches between être and avoir without conscious effort.

quiz.q: Saying 'je suis les cheveux longs' instead of 'j'ai les cheveux longs' is an example of ___.
opts: a sentence with no verb at all
a common mistake, using être where avoir is needed
an acceptable alternative with no error
quiz.explanation: Hair is a POSSESSED feature requiring avoir, not être. 'Je suis les cheveux longs' is incorrect.

quiz.q: How would you say 'I am honest and a little shy'?
opts: Je es honnête et un peu timide
Je suis honnête et un peu timides
Je suis honnête et un peu timide
J'ai honnête et un peu timide
quiz.explanation: 'Je suis' (être, first person) + adjectives. 'Timide' is unchanged in both genders and stays singular.

quiz.q: Combining être and avoir sentences smoothly within one description reflects ___.
opts: a lack of any real language skill
growing fluency built through repeated practice
a skill unrelated to overall language competence
an error that should always be avoided
quiz.explanation: Smooth switching between être and avoir in a single description is a clear sign of growing French fluency.

subUnits.title: 2.2 Révision: L'Accord des Adjectifs (Masculin/Féminin, Singulier/Pluriel)
notes: Révision: L'Accord des Adjectifs
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: consolidate and apply adjective agreement rules across combined physical and character vocabulary.
Key Concepts:
1. Agreement Review — Three Categories:
- UNCHANGING (already end in '-e'): timide, honnête, malhonnête, sympathique, rusée is NOT unchanging — check the ending carefully
- REGULAR '+e': intelligent → intelligente | grand → grande | petit → petite
- IRREGULAR: beau → belle (fully irregular, reviewed from JSS1)
2. Important Watch-Out:
- 'rusé' DOES change to 'rusée' (it ends in '-é', not '-e') — do not confuse '-é' with '-e'
- Always CHECK the actual spelling before assuming a word is unchanging.
3. Mixed Practice:
- True mastery means applying agreement across BOTH physical AND character vocabulary together.
Formula Box:
Unchanging: timide (m/f same) | honnête (m/f same)
Regular +e: intelligent → intelligente | grand → grande
Check: rusé (m.) → rusée (f.) — does NOT stay the same
Analogy:

Reviewing agreement across BOTH physical and character vocabulary is like a sports team practising with players from every position at once: true mastery only shows itself when ALL the skills are tested TOGETHER under mixed, realistic conditions.
Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- Assuming a word is unchanging just because it SOUNDS similar to others — always check the actual spelling/ending.
- Practising agreement with only ONE category of vocabulary instead of mixing physical and character words.

quiz.q: Does 'timide' change between masculine and feminine forms?
opts: Yes, it becomes 'timides' in the singular
quiz.explanation: 'Timide' already ends in '-e' and is therefore UNCHANGING — the same form for both masculine and feminine.

quiz.q: Does 'intelligent' change between masculine and feminine forms?
opts: No, it stays exactly the same
Yes, but only in the plural
quiz.explanation: 'Intelligent' does not end in '-e', so it takes the regular +e rule for the feminine: intelligente.

quiz.q: Does 'rusé' change between masculine and feminine forms?
opts: Yes, but only in speech, not writing
No, it stays the same, like 'timide'
quiz.explanation: 'Rusé' ends in '-é' (with an accent), NOT '-e' — it therefore DOES change: feminine is 'rusée.'

quiz.q: What should you always check before assuming an adjective is 'unchanging'?
opts: Only its meaning, never its spelling
Nothing; all similar-sounding words behave identically
Its actual spelling/ending, not just how it sounds
quiz.explanation: Always check the actual spelling — '-é' and '-e' look similar but behave differently for agreement.

quiz.q: What is the feminine form of 'petit'?
quiz.explanation: 'Petit' takes the regular +e rule for the feminine: petite.

quiz.q: Mixed practice combining physical and character vocabulary helps reveal ___.
opts: nothing useful about a student's progress
whether agreement rules are truly mastered, not just memorised narrowly
quiz.explanation: Mixing categories tests whether rules are truly mastered or only applied in narrow, familiar situations.

quiz.q: This week's analogy compares mixed-category review to ___.
opts: a team with no need for combined practice
a sports team practising with players from every position at once
a team that only ever trains one position
quiz.explanation: True team readiness requires all positions practising together — just as true French mastery requires all agreement rules applied together.

quiz.q: How would you correctly complete 'Elle est ___' with 'honnête'?
quiz.explanation: 'Honnête' already ends in '-e' and is unchanging — stays 'honnête' for all genders.

quiz.q: How would you correctly complete 'Il est ___' with 'rusé'?
quiz.explanation: 'Rusé' is the masculine form — it stays 'rusé' for a masculine subject. The feminine is 'rusée.'

quiz.q: True mastery of adjective agreement is best demonstrated by ___.
opts: correctly applying it across mixed, varied vocabulary
memorising just one single example sentence
quiz.explanation: Mastery means correctly applying agreement rules across all types of vocabulary, not just familiar examples.

weeklyAssessment.question: Rédigez une auto-description complète (4 phrases), combinant taille, cheveux, et deux traits de caractère.
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 1.25 marks per correctly formed, well-agreed sentence (4 sentences, 5 total).

weeklyAssessment.question: Expliquez pourquoi une description complète utilise à la fois 'être' et 'avoir,' avec un exemple de chaque.
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: Clear explanation (2.5); valid examples for both verbs (2.5).

weeklyAssessment.question: Donnez la forme féminine de: 'timide,' 'intelligent,' 'honnête,' 'rusé.'
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 1.25 marks per correctly formed (or correctly identified as unchanged) feminine form (4 items, 5 total).

weeklyAssessment.question: Expliquez pourquoi il est important de vérifier l'orthographe exacte d'un adjectif avant de supposer qu'il est invariable.
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: Clear, accurate explanation with reference to a specific example (5, holistic).

weeklyAssessment.question: Traduisez: 'I am tall and honest. She is short and a little shy. We are intelligent.'
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 1.67 marks per correctly translated, correctly agreed sentence (3 sentences, 5 total).
